t:
The Commissioner and the Director of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement shall include in the joint strategic plan required by section 105—
    (1) a description of the efforts of the Department of Homeland Security to enforce intellectual property rights; 
    (2) a list of the 10 United States ports of entry at which U.S. Customs and Border Protection has seized the most merchandise, both by volume and by value, that infringes intellectual property rights during the most recent 2-year period for which data are available; and 
    (3) a recommendation for the optimal allocation of personnel, resources, and technology to ensure that U.S. Customs and Border Protection and U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement are adequately enforcing intellectual property rights.

fable.w: The section only lists what two federal officials (the CBP Commissioner and the ICE Director) must include in a joint strategic plan: enforcement efforts, port seizure data, and a resource allocation recommendation. The tempting reading is that a "joint" plan and a "recommendation" imply consultation, but the coordination is entirely between federal agencies. No state, company, expert, or member of the public is consulted, and there is no rulemaking, hearing, or right to sue.
fable.s: The Commissioner and the Director of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement shall include in the joint strategic plan required by section 105

qwen_block.w: This section mandates that federal officials (the Commissioner and the Director of ICE) create a strategic plan containing specific internal data and recommendations. All actors involved are within the federal government (Department of Homeland Security, CBP, ICE). There is no requirement to consult with, coordinate with, or receive input from any outside parties such as the public, states, or private entities. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_block.s: The Commissioner and the Director of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement shall include in the joint strategic plan required by section 105— (1) a description of the efforts of the Department of Homeland Security to enforce intellectual property rights; (2) a list of the 10 United States ports of entry at which U.S. Customs and Border Protection has seized the most merchandise, both by volume and by value, that infringes intellectual property rights during the most recent 2-year period for which data are available; and (3) a recommendation for the optimal allocation of personnel, resources, and technology to ensure that U.S. Customs and Border Protection and U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement are adequately enforcing intellectual property rights.

opus.w: This section only lists what must go into a joint strategic plan written by the CBP Commissioner and the ICE Director. Both are federal officials, so the coordination stays inside the federal government. The words "joint" and "recommendation" might look like participation, but nobody outside the government (states, experts, companies or the public) is consulted or given a say in any decision.
opus.s: The Commissioner and the Director of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement shall include in the joint strategic plan required by section 105—

qwen_chat.w: This section requires federal officials (the Commissioner and the Director of ICE) to include specific information and recommendations in a joint strategic plan. All actors mentioned (Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement) are part of the federal government. There is no requirement to consult with or coordinate with any non-federal entities, such as states, tribes, the public, or private companies. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: The Commissioner and the Director of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement shall include in the joint strategic plan required by section 105— (1) a description of the efforts of the Department of Homeland Security to enforce intellectual property rights; (2) a list of the 10 United States ports of entry at which U.S. Customs and Border Protection has seized the most merchandise... and (3) a recommendation for the optimal allocation of personnel, resources, and technology...
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the plan involves "recommendations" for resource allocation, it implies some form of consultation or input from outside parties. However, the text only mandates that federal officials (the Commissioner and the Director) include these items in a plan. There is no requirement to consult with states, tribes, the public, or other non-federal entities. The actors involved are entirely within the federal government (Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement).
